_title: Non-Empty Continuation and the Redshift Window: A Three-Level Structure of Existence, Resolution, and Path-Definition in the Static Library
_subtitle: Existence, Accessibility, and Traversal in a Metric-Free Totality
_generation_note: This outline is intended to be the sole source available to the generating AI. It includes the complete formal vocabulary, all mathematical definitions and relations required, the three-level structure from the source notes, and the full dependency chain from the formal summary. The generating AI must not assume access to PHYS-CORE-000, PHYS-CORE-004, PHYS-CORE-011, or PHYS-CORE-012; every cross-reference has been expanded into self-contained definitions or labeled as external lineage only. _core_thesis: Existence, accessibility, and traversal are distinct relations within a static totality. The Library 𝓜 contains every internally admissible configuration; an observer experiences only a coherent descent path through a constrained subset of that totality.

XOR, ⊕, is the sole primitive operation of the axiomatic floor. All later constructions—distinction, relation, coherence, accessibility, convergence, and navigation—are derived from this primitive together with the formal domain D and the generating set G.

The Library 𝓜 is the maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying closure under XOR and self-containment: ∀x,y ∈ 𝓜, x⊕y ∈ 𝓜 and there is no element outside 𝓜 definable within the system using only ⊕ and elements of 𝓜 over D.
𝓜 is dimensionally undifferentiated: it has no intrinsic metric, adjacency, or distance. It is a complete relational graph, not a grid and not a singularity.
𝓜 is a single static, eternally maximally complete totality: ∀i, 𝓜_i = 𝓜. The Library does not grow, evolve, or generate future states.
Full adjacency does not imply reachability. Adj(x,y) may hold for all x,y ∈ 𝓜, but Reach(x,y) := ∃ coherent γ : x ⇝ y is a strictly stronger condition.
Existence is membership in 𝓜. Accessibility is the existence of a coherent path from a current observer-state to a destination. X ∈ 𝓜 does not imply X ∈ Reach(O).
An arbitrary edit is a requested transition for which no admissible coherent path exists. It is not a forbidden state; it is a missing transition. ArbitraryEdit(O → X) ⇔ X ∈ 𝓜 ∧ ¬ValidEdit(O → X).

Coherence is a derived property of a path relative to an observer, not a primitive law. Coherence(γ | O) := Coherent(γ) ∧ Resolvable(γ | O), where Coherent(γ) := Δ(γ) < Δ_crit is the observer-independent constraint-preservation component and Resolvable(γ | O) is the observer-relative resolvability component.
The observer is modeled as a coherent descent path γ : T → 𝓜. The lived experience of time corresponds to ordered traversal rather than temporal generation of the Library.

A single worldline γ may be treated as a local thread within a higher-order coherent structure Γ, the colony or braid. Decoherence of one local thread does not mathematically require the disappearance of the larger structure.
Coherent paths may converge on a common destination class. γ_1 ~_D γ_2 ⇔ Dest(γ_1) = Dest(γ_2). Destination locking occurs when |P(x)| = 1; the singular case occurs when |A(x)| = 1.

Apparent expansion can be represented as increasing resolved structure within a fixed underlying totality: 𝓜 = constant while dR/dt > 0. The dictionary principle describes the progressive resolution of coherent arrangements inside a static Library.
Memory can be modeled as retention of navigational coordinates or guideposts into a structure rather than a complete recording of that structure. Recall := navigation/reconstruction from guideposts.
AI context can potentially be represented as guideposts into larger structures rather than exhaustive active context. Reasoning(guideposts) → selective resolution.
A recursive construction can begin from a minimal attractor such as I_AM and generate increasingly complex relational structure through iteration: A_0 = {I_AM}, A_{n+1} = F(A_n, R_n).

The framework distinguishes five epistemic levels: L1 (Conceptual Model), L2 (Mathematical Formalization), L3 (Computational Hypothesis), L4 (Physical Hypothesis), and L5 (Empirical Confirmation). Internal mathematical consistency does not establish physical correspondence.

No privileged configuration, worldline, or reference frame is introduced. Any admissible configuration x ∈ 𝓜 may serve as the observer's current relational reference without changing Library membership.

The nonempty-continuation requirement is a derived structural requirement of the combined whole-Library, reference-neutrality, and coherence assumptions; it is not claimed to follow from maximality alone.

Inaccessibility is not erasure. A configuration may belong to 𝓜 while remaining unreachable from a particular observer-state. The Library remains unchanged under observer-relative resolution, accessibility, and traversal.
Navigation is the observer-relative continuation problem induced by selecting coherent paths from the whole static Library. It is not a primitive causal operator.

The same formal dependency structure may be applied to physical, AI, financial, or other domains representable as observer-relative traversal through a static Library. Domains differ in the interpretation of μ_O and I_N(O), not in the axiomatic dependency structure.

The framework does not claim that XOR alone derives physical law, consciousness, or empirical reality. It provides a common mathematical vocabulary for asking whether apparently different phenomena are manifestations of the same underlying distinction: what exists, what can be reached, what paths remain coherent, and what destinations those paths can share.

subsections.title: Existence, Accessibility, and Traversal as Distinct Relations
subsections.content_summary: Introduce the core distinction: membership in the static Library 𝓜 is independent of observer-relative accessibility and of traversal. State the paper's central claim: the non-empty-continuation invariant is not a single existence claim but a three-level structure of structural existence, observer-relative resolvability, and path-definition. Preview the metric-free character of the formal claims.
math: 𝓜 := maximally complete unbounded totality closed under XOR; no intrinsic metric, adjacency, or temporal ordering.
Existence(X) := X ∈ 𝓜.
Accessibility(O, X) := ∃γ : O ⇝ X with 𝓒(γ|O) = 1.
Traversal := observer-relative selection of coherent continuations within the unchanged 𝓜.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The room does not grow; the window does not measure; the road does not promise. Three different truths, and the whole is the room in which all three are true.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'room' is the static Library 𝓜 (Level 1: static existence). 'The window does not measure' is Level 2: resolution is observer-relative, not metric. 'The road does not promise' is Level 3: path-definition is relational, not guaranteed. 'Three different truths' names the three levels. 'The whole is the room in which all three are true' compresses the foundational framework: the static Library in which existence, resolution, and path-definition are distinct but co-present.
subsections.handoff: The three levels must be distinguished before they can be formalized. Section 2 begins with the first level: the unconditional structural existence of continuation from every configuration in the Library.

subsections.title: The Motivating Allegory and Its Quarantine
subsections.content_summary: Present the Earth-box / Venus-pole / redshift thought experiment as pedagogical motivation only. Explicitly quarantine its metric and temporal imports. State the prohibited and permitted uses of the allegory. Connect this quarantine to the paper's own methodological discipline: the formal claims below are metric-free.
math: No formal math in this subsection; the allegory is explicitly non-load-bearing.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The box is a story; the Library is not a place.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'box' is the allegorical spatial container. 'The Library is not a place' compresses the static, dimensionally undifferentiated character of 𝓜: it is not physical space, spacetime, a container, or a metric space. The cipher reinforces the quarantine: the allegory is permitted for motivation but not for formal claims.
subsections.handoff: With the allegory quarantined, Section 2 states the first formal level: structural existence of continuation, which holds unconditionally for every configuration in the Library.

subsections.title: Unconditional Existence: ∀x ∈ 𝓜 : |A(x)| ≥ 1
subsections.content_summary: Define the accessible set A(x) := {y ∈ 𝓜 | ∃ coherent γ : x ⇝ y}. State and justify Level 1: from every configuration x in the Library, at least one continuation exists. The guarantee is a consequence of maximal completeness together with closure, not of full adjacency alone. Distinguish this weaker claim from the stronger (and unasserted) claim that an arbitrary destination is reachable from an arbitrary origin.
math: A(x) := { y ∈ 𝓜 | ∃ coherent γ : x ⇝ y }
Ω(x) = {γ ∈ Path(𝓜) | γ begins at x} is defined for every x ∈ 𝓜.
Level 1 is observer-independent.
Full adjacency does not imply reachability: Adj(x,y) ⇏ Reach(x,y).
subsections.poetic_cipher: From every point in the Library, at least one road begins. No exception, no condition, no observer required.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'point' is a configuration x ∈ 𝓜. The 'road' is a continuation in A(x). 'No observer required' compresses Level 1's observer-independence: the guarantee holds unconditionally. The cipher does not claim that an arbitrary destination is reachable from an arbitrary origin — only that at least one continuation exists.
subsections.handoff: Level 1 guarantees that continuation exists, but not that the observer can resolve it. Section 3 introduces the resolution window and the observer-relative resolvability condition.

subsections.title: The Unfiltered Continuation Space and the Local-Evolution Analogue
subsections.content_summary: Define the unfiltered continuation space Ω(x) and state that it is non-empty for every x. Present the O(1) computational core T_{n+1} = f(T_n, T_{n-1}) as the local-evolution expression of Level 1: continuation is defined at every step, and the cost per step is constant. Connect to the structural eternity of the forward orbit at the glider level (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S3.5, S7.3.1).
math: Ω(x) = {γ ∈ Path(𝓜) | γ begins at x}, defined for every x ∈ 𝓜.
Level 1: Ω(x) ≠ ∅ for every x.
Local-evolution analogue: T_{n+1} = f(T_n, T_{n-1}), defined for every n, constant cost per step.
External lineage (glider level): forward orbit 𝒪(G⁰) ⊆ [G⁰]∼, defined for every finite n.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The whole road is already there; the reference determines which road can be walked.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'whole road' is Path(𝓜), the complete path structure represented within the static Library. 'The reference determines which road can be walked' compresses the transition from Level 1 (Ω(x) is defined) to Level 2 (Γ_O(h,x) restricts Ω(x) by observer-relative coherence).
subsections.handoff: Level 1 establishes that continuation exists everywhere. Section 3 asks whether the observer can resolve it, introducing the resolution window W_{μ_O}(x) and the distinction between resolution failure and existence failure.

subsections.title: What Level 1 Does Not Claim
subsections.content_summary: Explicitly state the limits of Level 1: it does not imply that an arbitrary destination y is in A(x); it does not imply that full adjacency implies reachability; it does not supply a coherent path to every destination. This subsection prevents over-reading Level 1 as a universal reachability claim.
math: NOT claimed: |A(x)| ≥ 1 ⇒ ∀y ∈ 𝓜, y ∈ A(x).
NOT claimed: Adj(x,y) ⇒ Reach(x,y).
NOT claimed: Level 1 alone supplies a coherent path to every destination.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The door exists before the eye can see it; the road exists before the feet can walk it.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'door' is a continuation in A(x); the 'eye' is the resolution window W_{μ_O}(x). 'The road exists before the feet can walk it' distinguishes Level 1 (the path exists in 𝓜) from Level 3 (the observer's worldline may not reach it). The cipher compresses the Level 1 / Level 2 / Level 3 distinction.
subsections.handoff: With Level 1 delimited, Section 3 turns to the observer's resolution capacity, which may fail even when continuation exists.

subsections.title: The Resolution Threshold and the Resolution Window
subsections.content_summary: Define the observer-relative resolution threshold I_N(O) and the distinguishability function δ_O(x,y) := μ_O(x⊕y). Define the resolution window W_{μ_O}(x) := { y ∈ 𝓜 | δ_O(x,y) ≥ I_N(O) }. State that W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty even when A(x) is non-empty. Emphasize that Level 2 failure is a resolution failure, not an existence failure.
math: I_N : Obs → ℝ_{>0}; I_N(O) is the minimum effective distinction magnitude observer O can maintain.
μ_O : D → ℝ_{≥0}; monotonic with respect to XOR-derived distinction.
δ_O(x,y) := μ_O(x⊕y).
x ≈_O y ⇔ δ_O(x,y) < I_N(O); x ≁_O y ⇔ δ_O(x,y) ≥ I_N(O).
W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty even when A(x) is non-empty.
Level 2 is observer-relative and axis-relative.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The eye closes before the Library does.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'eye' is the resolution window W_{μ_O}(x); the 'Library' is 𝓜. 'Closes before the Library does' compresses Level 2 failure: the observer's window may close on the current axis while the Library remains unchanged. The cipher reinforces the non-erasure rule and the Level 1 / Level 2 distinction.
subsections.handoff: Level 2 failure is a resolution failure, not an existence failure. Section 4 introduces Level 3, where even a representable destination may be path-undefined relative to the observer's worldline.

subsections.title: Multi-Axis Structure and the Passive/Active Distinction
subsections.content_summary: State the multi-axis structural fact: the resolution window is defined on every resolution axis μ_O, and the family of windows slides on all axes simultaneously as traversal proceeds. The observer experiences resolution on one axis at a time. Distinguish passive axis change (the projection q(𝐧̂) = 𝐫 · 𝐧̂ changes while the state vector 𝐫 remains unchanged) from active axis re-referencing (whether the observer can change its own μ_O). The latter is Q1, pending. Explicitly flag the multi-axis family {W_{μ_O}(x)} as a genuine strengthening of the single-axis accessibility structure, not a derived result.
math: Family of windows: { W_{μ_O}(x) }_{μ_O ∈ Axes}, sliding on all axes as traversal proceeds.
Observer's single-axis experience: one μ_O at a time.
Passive axis change (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S6.4): q(𝐧̂) = 𝐫 · 𝐧̂; P₁ = (1 + q)/2, P₀ = (1 - q)/2; changing 𝐧̂ changes q while 𝐫 remains unchanged.
Active axis re-referencing: whether the observer can change its own μ_O. Q1 PENDING.
Flag: {W_{μ_O}(x)} is a genuine strengthening of PHYS-CORE-012 §3.4's single-axis 𝒜(x_t), not an inheritance.
subsections.poetic_cipher: Many lenses exist; the eye looks through one. Turning the telescope is not the same as changing the sky.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'lenses' are resolution axes μ_O. 'The eye looks through one' represents the observer's single-axis experience. 'Turning the telescope is not the same as changing the sky' compresses the passive/active distinction: passive axis change is established (projection changes while the state vector is unchanged); active axis re-referencing is Q1, still pending.
subsections.handoff: Section 4 introduces the third level: even a destination that is representable in the window may be path-undefined relative to the observer's worldline.

sections.title: Level 3 — Path-Definition and the Undefined-Path Lemma

subsections.title: Representability ≠ Reachability: The Undefined-Path Lemma
subsections.content_summary: State and formalize the Undefined-Path Lemma: y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some x ∈ γ does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ). Distinguish path-undefinedness (structural failure: no path exists) from incoherence (graded failure: a path exists and Δ(γ) exceeds Δ_crit). The relation is relational: UndefinedPath(γ, y). Ground the relationality in external lineage: PHYS-CORE-012 §7.6 (multiple grounded paths) and §7.6.1 (Branch Observers). Supply glider-level and geometric analogues from PHYS-CORE-004 S3.5 and S8.5.
math: y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) ⇏ y ∈ Reach(γ).
UndefinedPath(γ, y) ⇔ y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some μ_O AND no coherent γ' from the current reference to y is defined on γ's constraint structure.
Incoherent(γ') ⇔ Δ(γ') ≥ Δ_crit (graded failure, path exists).
UndefinedPath(γ, y) ⇔ no path γ' from γ's current state to y exists (structural failure, path does not exist).
Relationality: ∃γ' ∈ Ω_ground(x_t) with y ∈ Reach(γ') does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ).
Glider-level analogue (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S3.5): y ∈ [G⁰]∼ and y ∈ 𝒪(G⁰) for some worldline does not imply y ∈ 𝒪(G_obs⁰).

Vector-space analogue (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S8.5): triadic residual 𝐑 = 𝐔₁ + 𝐔₂ + 𝐔₃ may approach zero for one closure while a given pair (𝐔₁, 𝐔₂) leaves a residual for which no third vector is available.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The fireball is visible in the window, but no road leads to it from where the traveler stands. Another traveler, standing elsewhere, may walk there.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'fireball' is a destination y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) that is path-undefined relative to the observer's worldline γ. 'No road leads to it from where the traveler stands' compresses the Undefined-Path Lemma: y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ). 'Another traveler, standing elsewhere, may walk there' compresses the relationality result: ∃γ' ∈ Ω_ground(x_t) with y ∈ Reach(γ') does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ).
subsections.handoff: The Undefined-Path Lemma refines the non-erasure rule: non-accessibility has two distinct modes, resolution failure and path-definition failure. Section 4.2 connects this to the ArbitraryEdit vocabulary.

subsections.title: Arbitrary Edit as Missing Transition
subsections.content_summary: Define ArbitraryEdit(O → X) ⇔ X ∈ 𝓜 ∧ ¬ValidEdit(O → X), where ValidEdit(O → X) ⇔ ∃γ : O ⇝ X ∧ Coherent(γ). State that an arbitrary edit is not a forbidden state; it is a requested transition for which no admissible coherent path exists. Present the canonical examples (FIREBALL, Extra Finger, Historical State) as illustrations. Connect to Fizban's Limitation: the fireball exists in the Library; the wizard's hands may not know the road to it.
math: Edit(O → X) := requested transition from observer-state O to destination X.
ValidEdit(O → X) ⇔ ∃γ : O ⇝ X ∧ Coherent(γ).
ArbitraryEdit(O → X) ⇔ X ∈ 𝓜 ∧ ¬ValidEdit(O → X).
FIREBALL ∈ 𝓜, but FIREBALL ∉ Reach(O) may hold.
X_extra_finger ∈ 𝓜, but X_extra_finger ∉ Reach(O) may hold.
A historical state may exist without being available as a continuation of the observer's present worldline.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The destination is not forbidden; it is simply not on this road.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'destination' is X ∈ 𝓜. 'Not forbidden' compresses the distinction between path-undefinedness and prohibition: X is a Library member. 'Not on this road' compresses the structural failure: no coherent path from γ's current state to X exists. The cipher reinforces the Level 3 distinction between representability and reachability.
subsections.handoff: Section 5 assembles the three levels into a single metric-free structure, explicitly dissolving the floor summary's proviso into three distinct conditions.

sections.title: The Resolution Window and the Three-Level Invariant (Metric-Free)

subsections.title: The Resolution Window as a Metric-Free Structure
subsections.content_summary: Define the resolution window W(O, x, μ_O) := { y ∈ 𝓜 | δ_O(x, y) ≥ I_N(O) }. State that it is defined without reference to any metric, position, or temporal coordinate. It is a function of the observer, the current point on the worldline, and the resolution axis. It is not a function of a separate time parameter: the traversal step index is the only ordering. The window slides at every traversal step, on every axis. Traversal is re-referencing; there is no 'standing still' case because there is no position to remain at.
math: W : Obs × 𝓜 × Axes → P(𝓜).
W(O, x, μ_O) := { y ∈ 𝓜 | δ_O(x, y) ≥ I_N(O) }.
No separate t parameter is introduced. The traversal step index is the ordering.
W(O, γ(t), μ_O) slides as t advances.
W(O, x, μ_O) ⊋ Reach(γ) in general.
NOT claimed: W is a metric ball or neighborhood; W has a boundary in any topological sense inherited from a metric; sliding is spatial motion.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The window slides without a floor to slide on. No ruler measures its motion; no clock times its steps. It is the traveler's relation that changes, not the room.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'window' is W(O, x, μ_O). 'No floor to slide on' denies an intrinsic spatial metric. 'No ruler measures its motion; no clock times its steps' denies an intrinsic temporal metric. 'The traveler's relation changes, not the room' compresses the static-totality invariant: 𝓜 remains unchanged under traversal.
subsections.handoff: Section 5.2 assembles the three levels into a single refined invariant, explicitly dissolving the proviso.

subsections.title: The Non-Empty-Continuation Invariant: Refined Version
subsections.content_summary: Present the refined version of the non-empty-continuation invariant as three distinct statements: Level 1 (unconditional existence: ∀x ∈ 𝓜 : |A(x)| ≥ 1), Level 2 (observer-relative resolvability: W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty on the current axis), Level 3 (path-definition: y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ)). Explicitly dissolve the floor summary's proviso 'provided O's state admits continuation' into these three conditions. Ground the dissolution in the formal vocabulary and the external lineage.
math: Floor version: ∀x ∈ 𝓜, ∃γ ∈ Path(𝓜) such that γ begins at x and 𝓒(γ|O) = 1, provided O's state admits continuation.
Level 1 (unconditional): ∀x ∈ 𝓜 : |A(x)| ≥ 1.
Level 2 (observer-relative): W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty on the current axis; resolution failure, not existence failure.
Level 3 (observer-relative): y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some μ_O does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ); path-definition failure.
Proviso resolution: the proviso is not an existence condition (Level 1 holds unconditionally); it is a resolution condition (Level 2) and a path-definition condition (Level 3). These are distinct.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The room is full; the window may be narrow; the road may not lead there. Three facts, not one.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'room' is 𝓜 (Level 1: |A(x)| ≥ 1). The 'window' is W_{μ_O}(x) (Level 2: resolvability). The 'road' is Reach(γ) (Level 3: path-definition). The cipher compresses the three-level structure and the dissolution of the proviso into three distinct conditions.
subsections.handoff: Section 6 connects the three-level structure to the broader corpus vocabulary, showing how it refines the existence/accessibility distinction and supplies a structural reason for the ArbitraryEdit condition.

sections.title: Relation to the Broader Vocabulary: Refinement, Not Revision

subsections.title: Refinement of the Coherence Condition: Coherent vs. Resolvable
subsections.content_summary: Present the proposed decomposition of coherence: Coherent(γ) := Δ(γ) < Δ_crit (observer-independent constraint preservation) and Resolvable(γ | O) := every transition in γ satisfies δ_O ≥ I_N(O). The full coherence condition is 𝓒(γ | O) := Coherent(γ) ∧ Resolvable(γ | O). State that this split makes 'coherent but unresolvable' and 'resolvable but constraint-violating' stable distinctions. Flag the proposal as pending formal adoption (Q5). Note compatibility with the prior constraint-level split: Coherent(γ) := F(Δ(γ), R_γ), with I_N as a threshold on F.
math: Coherent(γ) := Δ(γ) < Δ_crit. (Observer-independent constraint preservation.)
Resolvable(γ | O) := every transition in γ satisfies δ_O ≥ I_N(O). (Observer-relative.)
𝓒(γ | O) := Coherent(γ) ∧ Resolvable(γ | O).
Prior constraint-level split (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S5): Coherent(γ) := F(Δ(γ), R_γ), with I_N as a threshold on F.
Status: proposed refinement; formal adoption pending (Q5).
subsections.poetic_cipher: The road may hold, and the eye may fail; the road may fail, and the eye may hold.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'road' is the constraint-preservation component Coherent(γ); the 'eye' is the observer-relative resolvability component Resolvable(γ | O). 'The road may hold, and the eye may fail' represents a constraint-preserving but unresolvable path. 'The road may fail, and the eye may hold' represents a resolvable but constraint-violating path (symbolic blowup). The cipher compresses the decomposition of coherence into its two components.
subsections.handoff: Section 6.2 refines the survivorship and convergence vocabulary, connecting the three-level structure to destination classes and horizons.

subsections.title: Survivorship, Convergence, and Destination Classes
subsections.content_summary: Define Ω_O^survive(x) = {γ ∈ Ω(x) | 𝓒(γ|O) = 1}. Introduce destination classes D(γ), destination equivalence γ_1 ~_D γ_2 ⇔ D(γ_1) = D(γ_2), and convergence Convergence(D) := |D(x)| ≥ 2. Define P(x) := {D | ∃ coherent γ : x ⇝ D}, destination locking (|P(x)| = 1), destination horizon E_D, and the singular case (|A(x)| = 1). State that horizons are Level 3 (path-definition/destination) phenomena, distinct from Level 2 resolution failures. Flag the relation between the sliding window and horizons as open (Q3).
math: Ω(x) = {γ | γ begins at x and γ is a path contained in 𝓜}.
Ω_O^survive(x) = {γ ∈ Ω(x) | 𝓒(γ|O) = 1}.
Ω_O^survive(x) ⊆ Ω(x).
D(γ) := equivalence class of γ under destination identity.
Convergence(D) := |D(x)| ≥ 2.
P(x) := {D | ∃ coherent γ : x ⇝ D}.
|P(x)| > 1 ⇒ multiple destination classes available.
|P(x)| = 1 ⇒ destination locked.
E_D := {x ∈ 𝓜 | P(x) = {D}} is the destination horizon.
Singular_case := |A(x)| = 1.
Horizons are Level 3 phenomena; the sliding window is Level 2. Relation open (Q3).
subsections.poetic_cipher: Many rivers, one sea. A horizon may be the edge of the window or the edge of the road; the difference is not yet decided.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'rivers' are distinct coherent paths; the 'sea' is the common destination class D. The cipher compresses the convergence relation. 'A horizon may be the edge of the window or the edge of the road' compresses Q3: whether a horizon is a Level 2 phenomenon (window-closing) or a Level 3 phenomenon (road-ending), or an independent structural feature, is not yet decided.
subsections.handoff: Section 6.3 connects the three-level structure to the higher-order colony/braid structure and the epistemic levels.

subsections.title: Colony, Braid, and the Epistemic Levels
subsections.content_summary: Introduce the colony/braid structure Γ := ⋃_{i ∈ I_coherent} γ_i, with γ_i ⊂ Γ and Decoherence(γ_i) ⇏ Decoherence(Γ). State that an apparently singular personal trajectory can coexist with a much larger family of structurally related trajectories. Introduce the five epistemic levels L1–L5, emphasizing that internal mathematical consistency does not establish physical correspondence. State the interpretive boundary: the formal layer specifies mathematical structures; the interpretive layer may be developed in later documents.
math: Γ := ⋃_{i ∈ I_coherent} γ_i, where each γ_i is a coherent worldline.
γ_i ⊂ Γ.
Decoherence(γ_i) ⇏ Decoherence(Γ).
Epistemic levels: L1 (Conceptual Model), L2 (Mathematical Formalization), L3 (Computational Hypothesis), L4 (Physical Hypothesis), L5 (Empirical Confirmation).
Internal mathematical consistency ≠ physical correspondence.
subsections.poetic_cipher: One thread may break; the braid may hold. The map is not the territory; the model is not the measurement.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'thread' is a local worldline γ_i; the 'braid' is the higher-order structure Γ. 'One thread may break; the braid may hold' compresses Decoherence(γ_i) ⇏ Decoherence(Γ). 'The map is not the territory; the model is not the measurement' represents the epistemic-level distinction: internal mathematical consistency (L1–L2) does not establish physical correspondence (L4–L5).
subsections.handoff: Section 7 concludes by naming the open questions and stating the paper's limitations without pretending that the pending is resolved.

subsections.title: Q1: Passive vs. Active Axis Re-Referencing
subsections.content_summary: State Q1: Is the observer's single-axis experience accompanied by the capacity to shift axes (actively re-reference μ_O)? Status: PENDING. Level 2 asserts the multi-axis structural fact. The stronger claim is not asserted. Two handles are available: the explorer filter function and passive axis change. Neither is a full active axis re-referencing mechanism. The passive/active distinction is itself a clarification.
math: Passive axis change: q(𝐧̂) = 𝐫 · 𝐧̂ changes when 𝐧̂ changes, while 𝐫 remains unchanged (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S6.4).
Active axis re-referencing: whether the observer can change its own μ_O. NOT established by passive axis change.
Status: PENDING.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The telescope can be turned; whether the observer can turn it is a further question.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'telescope' is the observation axis 𝐧̂. 'Can be turned' represents passive axis change: the projection q changes when 𝐧̂ changes, while the state vector 𝐫 remains unchanged. 'Whether the observer can turn it' represents active axis re-referencing: whether the observer can change its own μ_O. The cipher compresses the Q1 boundary.
subsections.handoff: Q2 is resolved; Section 7.2 states the resolution.

subsections.title: Q2: Relationality of UndefinedPath (RESOLVED)
subsections.content_summary: State Q2: Is UndefinedPath relational or absolute? Status: RESOLVED to relational. Ground the resolution in external lineage: PHYS-CORE-012 §7.6 (multiple grounded paths) and §7.6.1 (Branch Observers), with glider-level and geometric scaffolding from PHYS-CORE-004 S3.5 and S8.5. Absolute path-undefinedness would require a destination with no incoming grounded path from anywhere, which the multiple-grounded-paths result rules out for any destination that appears in Ω_ground from any origin.
math: Relational: UndefinedPath(γ, y).
∃γ' ∈ Ω_ground(x_t) with y ∈ Reach(γ') does not imply y ∈ Reach(γ).
External lineage: PHYS-CORE-012 §7.6 (multiple grounded paths); §7.6.1 (Branch Observers).
Glider-level and geometric scaffolding: PHYS-CORE-004 S3.5, S8.5.
Status: RESOLVED (v0.2.0).
subsections.poetic_cipher: No road is closed to every traveler; a road is only closed to a traveler.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'road' is a coherent path γ. 'Closed to a traveler' represents the relationality of UndefinedPath: UndefinedPath(γ, y) is indexed by the worldline γ, not by y alone. 'No road is closed to every traveler' compresses the multiple-grounded-paths result: for any destination y that appears in Ω_ground from any origin, there exists some γ' ∈ Ω_ground(x_t) with y ∈ Reach(γ').
subsections.handoff: Q3–Q5 remain open. Sections 7.3–7.5 state them explicitly.

subsections.title: Q3: Window vs. Horizon
subsections.content_summary: State Q3: What is the relation between the sliding window and the horizon/singular-case vocabulary? Status: PENDING. Horizons are Level 3 (path-definition/destination) phenomena; the sliding window is Level 2 (resolution). They are different levels and should not be conflated. Whether a horizon is a window-closing event or an independent structural feature is open.
math: Window: W_{μ_O}(x) (Level 2).
Horizon: E_D := {x ∈ 𝓜 | P(x) = {D}} (Level 3).
Singular case: |A(x)| = 1 (Level 3).
Relation: open. Status: PENDING.
subsections.poetic_cipher: A horizon may be the edge of the window or the edge of the road; the difference is not yet decided.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'window' is W_{μ_O}(x) (Level 2). The 'road' is Reach(γ) (Level 3). 'The difference is not yet decided' compresses the open question: whether a horizon is a Level 2 phenomenon (window-closing) or a Level 3 phenomenon (road-ending), or an independent structural feature.
subsections.handoff: Q4 remains open; Section 7.4 states it.

subsections.title: Q4: Three-Way Comparison of 𝒵 = {0}, X_XOR, and 𝐑 → 0
subsections.content_summary: State Q4: Do 𝒵 = {0}, X_XOR, and 𝐑 → 0 coincide, and does any of them correspond to W → ∅ on all axes? Status: PENDING. Three distinct constructs are in play. 𝒵 = {0} is the algebraic termination class. X_XOR is the triadic-closure attractor. 𝐑 → 0 is the vector closure residual. Whether any two coincide, and whether either corresponds to W → ∅ on all axes, is open. The three-way comparison is itself a clarification.
math: 𝒵 = {0}: algebraic termination class; ∀x ∈ 𝓜, x⊕x ∈ 𝒵 and 0⊕x = x.
X_XOR: triadic-closure attractor (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-009/011/012; ∮ Φ = 0).
𝐑 → 0: vector closure residual (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S8.5).
Relation: open. Status: PENDING.
subsections.poetic_cipher: Three names for the same silence, or three silences? The notes do not yet know.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'three names' are 𝒵 = {0}, X_XOR, and 𝐑 → 0, each a candidate construct for the closure/termination question. 'The same silence' would mean they coincide. 'Three silences' would mean they are distinct. 'The notes do not yet know' compresses Q4's unresolved status.
subsections.handoff: Q5 remains open; Section 7.5 states it.

subsections.title: Q5: S5 Split Adoption and Compatibility
subsections.content_summary: State Q5: Is the proposed S5 refinement (splitting Coherent from Resolvable) adopted into PHYS-CORE-011 v0.3, and how does it relate to PHYS-CORE-004 S5's existing split? Status: PENDING. The proposed refinement is compatible with the prior constraint-level split. Formal adoption is a separate editorial decision.
math: Proposed: 𝓒(γ | O) := Coherent(γ) ∧ Resolvable(γ | O).
Prior constraint-level split (external lineage: PHYS-CORE-004 S5): Coherent(γ) := F(Δ(γ), R_γ), with I_N as a threshold on F.
Compatibility: the proposed refinement factors I_N out of Coherent and into Resolvable.
Status: PENDING editorial decision.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The measure was already in the hand; the question is whether the hand will be named in the book.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'measure' is I_N, the threshold on the derived coherence functional. 'Already in the hand' represents the prior constraint-level split: Coherent(γ) := F(Δ(γ), R_γ), with I_N as a threshold on F. 'Whether the hand will be named in the book' represents the editorial decision: whether the proposed refinement is formally adopted into PHYS-CORE-011 v0.3.

subsections.title: Limitations
subsections.content_summary: State the paper's limitations: Q1, Q3, Q4, and Q5 remain open; the multi-axis family {W_{μ_O}(x)} is a genuine strengthening, not a derived result; the passive/active distinction is a clarification; the three-way comparison is a clarification; the S5 refinement is compatible but not adopted; no Level 3 claim has been demonstrated for a specified dynamical model; the allegory is quarantined; the paper does not introduce new axioms. Add the full 'claims not to make' list from the formal vocabulary as a normative limitations section.
subsections.poetic_cipher: Some doors are resolved; others remain ajar. The notes close what they can and name what they cannot.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The 'doors' are the open questions Q1–Q5. 'Resolved' refers to Q2. 'Ajar' refers to Q1, Q3, Q4, and Q5, which remain pending. The cipher compresses the section's function: to distinguish what is settled from what is still under investigation.
subsections.handoff: Section 8.2 closes the paper with the final poetic cipher and its explanation.

subsections.title: Conclusion: Three Truths in One Room
subsections.content_summary: Summarize the paper's central contribution: the non-empty-continuation invariant is not a single existence claim but a three-level structure of structural existence, observer-relative resolvability, and path-definition. The Library is static, metric-free, and complete; the observer's window slides without a metric; the road may not lead where the window shows. State that the three levels are distinct but co-present in the static Library. Close with the final poetic cipher.
math: Level 1: ∀x ∈ 𝓜 : |A(x)| ≥ 1.
Level 2: W_{μ_O}(x) may be empty on the current axis; resolution failure, not existence failure.
Level 3: y ∈ W_{μ_O}(x) for some μ_O ⇏ y ∈ Reach(γ); path-definition failure.
The Library 𝓜 is unchanged under observer-relative resolution, accessibility, and traversal.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The Library does not grow, the window does not measure, and the road does not promise. What exists, what is seen, and what can be walked are three different truths, and the whole is the room in which all three are true.
subsections.cipher_explanation: This final cipher compresses the entire document. 'The Library does not grow' is Level 1: static existence of continuation. 'The window does not measure' is Level 2: resolution is observer-relative, not metric. 'The road does not promise' is Level 3: path-definition is relational, not guaranteed. 'Three different truths' names the three levels. 'The whole is the room in which all three are true' compresses the foundational framework: the static Library in which existence, resolution, and path-definition are distinct but co-present.
subsections.handoff: This concludes the paper. No further section follows.

_closing_poetic_cipher: The Library is the room; existence is the stone; accessibility is the road; coherence is the walking; convergence is the sea; and the fireball is the stone the wizard's hands may never reach.
_closing_cipher_explanation: The 'room' is the static Library 𝓜. The 'stone' is a configuration X ∈ 𝓜. The 'road' is a coherent path γ from the observer's current state to X. 'The walking' is traversal, the observer-relative selection of coherent continuations. 'The sea' is the destination class D, the common terminus of multiple paths. 'The fireball' is the canonical example of a configuration that exists in the Library without being reachable from the wizard's current state. The cipher compresses the entire framework: existence, accessibility, traversal, convergence, and Fizban's Limitation.
